model_comparison.scope: Stochastic body, topology, textures and own clips differ; the baseline also has the semantic UV1 collar colour repair. No polygon-only cost or causal visual claim.

findings: Standard is nearly unchanged in this observation: GPU 11.102 versus 11.155 ms; Game 5.365 versus 5.382 ms; frame mean 40.079 versus 40.266 ms; CSV rate 24.951 versus 24.835 Hz.

Comic records higher GPU and frame cost in this observation: GPU 11.180 versus 10.557 ms (+0.623 ms); frame mean 40.660 versus 39.696 ms (+0.963 ms), with frame p95 51.642 versus 45.995 ms. A single sequential comparison does not establish a reproducible regression or equivalence.
High-detail motion callbacks average 0.446/0.462 ms, with maxima 0.820/0.774 ms for Standard/Comic. Sample averages 0.282/0.295 ms and is already included; costs must not be added.
Corrected fixture counts match each corresponding baseline: Standard 110 residents/44 cars and 1100/1382 components; Comic 110/45 and 1100/1413. Warm and completion checkpoints all pass.

Both high-detail runs retain long editor waiting: Game EventWait 34.762/35.286 ms and Slate DrawPrePass 35.981/36.548 ms. These costs continue to limit observed editor cadence near 25 Hz despite MaxFPS 60.

The earlier trace establishes FlushRenderingCommands and render/frame synchronization as the enclosing wait owner. This analysis does not capture a new callstack or identify the triggering window/callsite or pending render/RHI operation.

Native high-detail selection precedes fixture overrides, its own skeleton/clips and one material match, live material override count is zero, UV0 is used for all maps and mapped normal strength is 1.0. Face and finger articulation remain absent.
